page: Vultr vc2-24c-96gb is a General Purpose virtual server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 24 vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 96.0 GB of system memory, which yields a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 1600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU acceleration is present on this server type.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by average multi-core capabilities and weaker single-core execution. The shared CPU allocation model introduces potential resource contention, which is reflected in the weak single-core Geekbench score of 1094.0 and weak single-threaded gzip compression of 23.37 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks show average performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8547.0 and a passmark CPU score of 29089.76. Memory bandwidth remains stable, reaching 114.95 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. Qualitatively, this shared-CPU instance offers high resource density and a cost-effective option for workloads that can leverage parallel execution without requiring dedicated, sustained single-core performance.

This server configuration is suited for multi-threaded applications that benefit from high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage. Appropriate workloads include database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate multi-threaded data processing. It can also handle light machine learning tasks, such as LLM inference with small to medium models, where it achieves 80.89 tokens per second for a 135M model and 9.96 tokens per second for a 7B model. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring guaranteed, non-shared CPU performance.
